page: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It includes 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration bundled with this instance, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 2989.08, while its multi-core performance falls into the bottom 25% at the same score due to the physical core limitation. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show weaker results, with read-only large block transfers at 31.17 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 21.04 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels.

Given its hardware profile, the m6a.large is suited for general-purpose workloads that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-threaded processing. It is appropriate for basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications. However, it exhibits poor performance in database operations, software compilation, and multi-core tasks, making it less suitable for heavy database hosting or complex parallel computing.
